# Sirach Chapter 22 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 22 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**22:1** A sluggard is like a stone covered with filth, and everyone will hiss at his disgrace.

**22:2** A sluggard is like the dung of a dunghill; anyone who picks it up shakes it off his hand.

**22:3** It is a disgrace to a father to beget an undisciplined son; a foolish daughter is born to his loss.

**22:4** A prudent daughter will secure a husband; one who brings shame is a grief to her father.

**22:5** A brazen woman disgraces both father and husband; she will be despised by both.

**22:6** A speech at an unseasonable time is like music at a funeral; but a rod of discipline and instruction are wisdom at every time.

**22:7** Teaching a fool is like gluing together broken pottery, or rousing someone from a deep sleep.

**22:8** Whoever recounts a matter to a fool speaks to one who is drowsy, and at the end he will say, "What is it?"

**22:9** Weep for the dead, for the light has failed; and weep for the fool, for understanding has failed. Weep more softly for the dead, for he has found rest; but the life of a fool is worse than death.

**22:10** Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for a fool and an ungodly man it lasts all the days of their lives.

**22:11** Do not talk at length with a foolish person, and do not visit one without understanding. Guard yourself from him, lest you have trouble, and you will not be defiled in his collision. Avoid him and you will find rest, and you will not grow weary in his folly.

**22:12** What is heavier than lead? And what is its name if not "Fool"?

**22:13** Sand and salt and a lump of iron are easier to bear than a man without understanding.

**22:14** Like beams of timber bound together in a building that an earthquake will not shake loose — so also a heart established upon well-reasoned counsel.

**22:15** A thought established upon intelligent understanding is like fine plasterwork on a smooth wall.

**22:16** Small stones placed on a high place will not hold back against the wind; so a timid heart in the imagination of a fool will not hold back against fear.

**22:17** A heart wounded by discernment is like a heart that has struck against a wall. It will not stand firm against any fear.

**22:18** A heart established upon an intelligent reflection is like plasterwork on a smooth wall.

**22:19** As pebbles thrown at birds will scare them away, so reproach heaped upon a friend dissolves a friendship.

**22:20** Even if you have drawn a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way back. Even if you have opened your mouth against a friend, do not be afraid, for reconciliation is possible. But insult and arrogance and betrayal of a secret and a treacherous blow — in these a friend will flee.

**22:21** Be faithful to your neighbor in his poverty, that you may also rejoice in his prosperity. Stand by him in the time of his affliction, that you may be an heir in his inheritance.

**22:22** Before fire there is vapor and smoke from the furnace; so before bloodshed there are insults.

**22:23** I will not be ashamed to shelter a friend, nor hide from his face.

**22:24** And if any evil happens to me because of him, everyone who hears will beware of him.

**22:25** Who will set a guard over my mouth and a seal upon my lips, so that I do not fall because of them and my tongue does not destroy me?

**22:26** O LORD, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel, and do not let me fall because of them.

**22:27** Who will assign a whip for my thoughts and discipline of wisdom over my heart, that they may not spare me in my ignorances, and that my sins may not be overlooked?
